howTo.name: How to pray salah, step by step
howTo.description: The eight positions of one rak'ah of salah in order, with what to say in each one.

mast.subtitle: Your five daily prayers
mast.lede: Here are the eight positions of salah, in the order you'll do them. Each one shows what your body should be doing and what to say while you're there. Going through all eight makes one rak'ah.

flow.name: One rak'ah
flow.sentence: Stand, Bow, Stand, Prostrate, Sit, Prostrate

takbir.title: Standing: takbir
takbir.caption: Hands raised, then folded
takbir.instruction: Stand facing the qiblah. Raise your hands to shoulder height or ear level, say the takbir, then fold your hands on your chest or stomach. From here, you're in prayer.

step.name: Standing: takbir
step.text: Stand facing the qiblah, raise your hands to shoulder or ear level, say Allahu akbar, then fold your hands on your chest or stomach.

qiyam.title: Standing: recitation
qiyam.caption: Eyes to the place of sujud
qiyam.instruction: Keep standing with your hands folded. In the first rak'ah only, say the opening supplication quietly. Then seek refuge, say the basmalah, and recite Al-Fatihah. You do this in every rak'ah, and nothing else takes its place. In the first two rak'ahs, add a short surah after Al-Fatihah.

lines.tr: Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabaraka-smuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk.

lines.meaning: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You."

lines.when: Then seeking refuge and the basmalah

lines.meaning: "I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful."

lines.tr: Then say: آمِين Amin

lines.meaning: "All praise is for Allah, Lord of all worlds, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who earned anger, nor of those who went astray."

lines.when: First two rak'ahs: a short surah (Al-Ikhlas)

lines.tr: Qul huwa Allahu ahad. Allahu-s-samad. Lam yalid wa lam yulad. Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad.

lines.meaning: "Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him."

step.name: Standing: recitation
step.text: In the first rak'ah, say the opening supplication quietly. Then seek refuge, say the basmalah and recite Al-Fatihah. In the first two rak'ahs, add a short surah after it.

ruku.title: Bowing
ruku.caption: Back flat, hands on knees
ruku.instruction: Say the takbir and bow. Bend from your hips until your back is flat, with your head in line with it. Spread your fingers on your knees, keep your arms and back straight, and get still before you speak.

lines.meaning: "Glory to my Lord, the Most Great." Three times, quietly.

step.name: Bowing (ruku)
step.text: Say the takbir and bow until your back is flat with your hands on your knees, then say Subhana Rabbiya-l-'Adhim three times.

itidal.title: Rising from the bow
itidal.caption: Upright, arms at the sides
itidal.instruction: Stand back up fully, saying the words as you rise. Pause here. This isn't just a movement, it's a position on its own.

lines.tr: Hamdan kathiran tayyiban mubarakan fih, mil'a-s-samawati wa mil'a-l-ardi wa mil'a ma shi'ta min shay'in ba'd.

lines.meaning: "Abundant, pure, blessed praise, filling the heavens, filling the earth, and filling whatever else You will."

step.name: Rising from the bow
step.text: Stand back up fully saying Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah, then say Rabbana wa laka-l-hamd once upright.

sujud.title: Prostration
sujud.caption: Seven points touch the ground
sujud.instruction: Say the takbir and go down. Your forehead, nose, both palms, both knees, and the toes of both feet should all be on the ground, seven points in all. Keep your elbows off the floor and away from your sides.

lines.meaning: "Glory to my Lord, the Most High." Three times, quietly.
"Perfect, Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit."

sujud.aside: After the required tasbih, this is the place to ask for whatever you want, in any language.

step.name: Prostration (sujud)
step.text: Say the takbir and go down so your forehead, nose, palms, knees and toes touch the ground, then say Subhana Rabbiya-l-A'la three times.

jalsa.title: Sitting between prostrations
jalsa.caption: Sitting back on the folded feet
jalsa.instruction: Say the takbir and sit up. Fold your left foot under you and sit on it, keep your right foot upright with toes pointing toward the qiblah, and rest your hands on your thighs. Get settled before moving on.

lines.tr: Rabbi-ghfir li, warhamni, wajburni, warfa'ni, warzuqni, wahdini, wa 'afini

lines.meaning: "My Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, mend me, raise me, provide for me, guide me, and grant me wellbeing."

step.name: Sitting between prostrations
step.text: Say the takbir and sit back on your folded left foot with your hands on your thighs, and say Rabbi-ghfir li.

sujud-2.title: Second prostration
sujud-2.caption: Identical to the first
sujud-2.instruction: Say the takbir and prostrate again exactly as before, with the same tasbih. That completes one rak'ah. Say the takbir and stand for the next one. After an even number of rak'ahs, stay seated for the tashahhud instead.

step.name: Second prostration
step.text: Say the takbir and prostrate again exactly as before. That completes one rak'ah.

tashahhud.title: Final sitting and salam
tashahhud.caption: Index finger raised at the shahadah
tashahhud.instruction: Sit like you did in stage 6 and recite the tashahhud, raising your index finger when you say the testimony of faith. In the last sitting, add the durood and a du'a. Then turn your head right and left with the salam. That's it, your prayer is done.

lines.note: then, in the final sitting: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad... and a du'a

lines.tr: At-tahiyyatu lillahi wa-s-salawatu wa-t-tayyibat. As-salamu 'alayka ayyuha-n-Nabiyyu wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. As-salamu 'alayna wa 'ala 'ibadillahi-s-salihin. Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh.

lines.meaning: "All greetings, prayers, and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and Allah's mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger."

lines.tr: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa 'ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta 'ala Ibrahima wa 'ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid.
Allahumma barik 'ala Muhammadin wa 'ala ali Muhammad, kama barakta 'ala Ibrahima wa 'ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid.

lines.meaning: "O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious."

lines.tr: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min 'adhabi jahannam, wa min 'adhabi-l-qabr, wa min fitnati-l-mahya wa-l-mamat, wa min sharri fitnati-l-Masihi-d-Dajjal.

lines.meaning: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the false messiah."
Twice: to the right, then to the left

step.name: Final sitting and salam
step.text: Sit and recite the tashahhud. In the last sitting add the salawat and a du'a, then turn your head right and left saying As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah.

counts.title: How many rak'ahs in each prayer

maghrib.name: Maghrib
maghrib.note: First two rak'ahs aloud, third quiet

isha.name: 'Isha
isha.note: First two rak'ahs aloud, last two quiet

counts.aside: Add a short surah after Al-Fatihah in the first two rak'ahs only. After every two rak'ahs, sit for the tashahhud. In Fajr, that sitting is also the final one.

footer.note: Some details vary between schools, like the opening supplication, saying Amin aloud or quietly, and where qunut fits in. All of these are within accepted practice. For pronunciation, listen to a reciter rather than relying on transliteration alone.
